papers_read.title_as_printed: Multiscale convolution-attention model for efficient Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment diagnosis approach using sMRI (Khatri, Kim & Kwon, Applied Soft Computing 184 (2025) 113693)

Automated classification of Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, and cognitively normal patients using 3D convolutional neural network and radiomic features from T1-weighted brain MRI: A comparative study on detection accuracy (Zarei et al., Clinical Imaging 115 (2024) 110301)

what_each_reports.P-109: BrainViT hybrid CNN-Transformer on 2D slices (about 50 axial/coronal/sagittal slices per subject, 54,300 slices) from ADNI 3T T1 MRI of 1075 subjects (390 AD, 370 MCI, 315 HC); 'The images were shuffled randomly' and split 90/10 train/test (slice level). Three-class AD/MCI/HC: BrainViT-L accuracy 96.81%, AUC 98.05 (Table 3). Binary: AD/HC 97.13% (AUC 98.52), MCI/HC 94.23% (AUC 97.15) (Table 4). No AD vs MCI binary result; no external cohort.
what_each_reports.P-66: ADNI 1.5T T1 MRI, 599 subjects (199 AD, 200 MCI, 200 CN; 2403 images), FSL-FIRST hippocampus and amygdala ROIs, radiomics + 3D CNN fusion, 5-fold CV with random image-level partitioning. Fusion: AD vs CN accuracy 84.4% (AUC 0.90); MCI vs CN 72.7% (AUC 0.80); AD vs MCI 58% (AUC 0.595) (Tables 5-7). Authors attribute poor AD vs MCI separation to the mild AD cases in ADNI.

quantity_a: Slice-level-split test accuracy/AUC of a whole-brain 2D-slice hybrid transformer for three-class AD/MCI/HC (and binary AD/HC, MCI/HC) in an ADNI 3T subset.
quantity_b: Image-level 5-fold CV accuracy/AUC of hippocampus+amygdala ROI radiomics/3D-CNN models for binary AD/CN, MCI/CN and AD/MCI in an ADNI 1.5T subset.
incompatible_if_same: The record sets P-109's three-class 96.81% against P-66's AD-vs-MCI separability; these are different tasks and P-109 reports no AD-vs-MCI binary figure. On the nearest shared task (MCI vs HC), 94.23% vs 72.7% +- 3.3 differ widely, but they come from different input representations (whole-brain slices vs two segmented ROIs), different scanner field strengths and ADNI subsets, and different split units. Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: mismatch for the recorded comparison: three-class staging (P-109) vs binary AD-vs-MCI (P-66). Partial match only on the binary MCI/HC and AD/HC tasks both report.
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (different subsets: P-109 3T; P-66 1.5T Siemens Symphony protocol).
gates.validation_tier: match in tier (internal only), but the split unit differs (random slice-level 90/10 split vs random image-level 5-fold CV); both are at risk of subject overlap between train and test.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible for the recorded pair (three-class accuracy vs binary AD/MCI accuracy); for MCI/HC the metric types match but the input representation differs (whole-brain 2D slices vs hippocampal/amygdala ROI radiomics and ROI CNN), the representation confound that reclassified precedent C-80.
performance_validity: flag applies to P-109 in substance, although the pack marks it false: AUC 98.05 (three-class), 98.52 (AD/HC) and 97.15 (MCI/HC) on internal validation only, with randomly shuffled slices (about 50 per subject) split 90/10, so slices from the same subject can appear in train and test; the sample (1075) is not small, so the automatic small-sample criterion is not met, but no external cohort exists. Any performance comparison resting on these figures cannot be genuine.
independence: Distinct author groups (Korea vs Iran); both draw ADNI participants, so overlap is possible but not determinable.
grounds: The recorded comparison sets P-109's three-class AD/MCI/HC accuracy against P-66's binary AD-vs-MCI result; P-109 reports no binary AD-vs-MCI figure, so the task gate fails.

On the binary tasks both report, the input representation differs (whole-brain 2D slices vs two segmented ROIs), as do field strength and ADNI subset, so the gap confounds representation and data with method.
Neither paper claims an ordering that the other refutes.
P-109's near-ceiling internal AUCs rest on a random slice-level split without an external cohort, so it would be excluded from any cross-study performance comparison.

evidence_quotes.quote: The images were shuffled randomly, and all experiments were carried out by splitting the data into 10 % for testing and 90 % for training.
For training and testing, around 50 brain fields—axial, coronal, and sagittal—were created from each subject's anatomy.
BrainViT-L, exhibited higher accuracy, surpassing other models, with rates of 97.13 % with 98.52 % AUC for AD/HC and 94.23 % with 97.15 % for MCI/HC classifications
we aimed to develop an algorithm based on CNN and radiomic features derived from ROIs of bilateral hippocampus and amygdala in brain MRI for stratification between AD, MCI and CN.

In the term of AD vs MCI, radiomic-based algorithm alone obtained ACC of 57 % and AUC of 57.5, CNN-based algorithm obtained ACC of 56.6 % and AUC of 57.7 and their fusion showed ACC of 58 % and AUC of 59.5.
The major limitation of this study was the single-center limitation.

record_defects: apparent_performance_gap '96.81% vs ~82% class-level comparables': no 82% figure appears in P-66 (its results are 84.4% AD/CN, 72.7% MCI/CN, 58% AD/MCI), and 96.81% is a three-class result.
claim_a describes 96.81% as 'AD/MCI diagnostic performance'; it is three-class AD/MCI/HC accuracy.
validation_tier_comparable true without noting that both evaluations split at image/slice level rather than subject level.
The pack's performance_suspect false for P-109 misses AUCs of 97-98.5 on internal validation only.
resolution_status false_positive with bridging evidence: the listed papers are unrelated headline scores; the correct ground is incommensurable tasks and representations.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A subject-level evaluation of both pipelines on the same ADNI subset for the same binary task, with one result's uncertainty excluding the other's, would make this a comparable quantity; P-109 would also need an external or subject-disjoint evaluation to escape the performance-validity exclusion.
